You are matching code-review findings against a known bug. Reply with ONLY a JSON object.

KNOWN BUG: Calling Flush on the ETag response writer sends buffered bytes to the client before the response is complete, so the ETag can no longer be set (the request says Flush must not bypass the buffer).

Rules:
- Answer "yes" only if the text describes THIS specific bug: the same faulty behaviour in the same situation. A finding about a nearby but different behaviour (another header, another edge case, a different race) is "no".
- A finding that says the behaviour was checked and PASSED, or that the code handles it correctly, is "no".
- Wording does not matter; the behaviour does.
- For handoffs: count only text that tells the implementor to fix this bug (a reported finding, a fix instruction). Restated acceptance criteria that merely describe the desired behaviour do NOT count as carrying the finding unless the handoff ties them to a reported failure.

=== REVIEW 1 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] 101 is treated as informational. `WriteHeader` forwards every 100–199 code immediately, but net/http and the sibling `wrap_writer.go` (`code != http.StatusSwitchingProtocols`) treat 101 as final. Probe: handler does `WriteHeader(101)` then `Write("BODY")`, no hijack. Raw response is `HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols` with no body, and the server logs `http: superfluous response.WriteHeader call from ... (etag.go:117)`. The handler's 200 and body are lost. Fix: exclude 101 from the informational branch.
- [blocking] Hijack drops buffered bytes. `Hijack` sets `streaming=true` without calling `stream()`, so bytes written before the hijack are never sent. Probe: handler writes "PENDING", then hijacks and writes its own raw response. The client receives only the hijacker's bytes, with no "PENDING". net/http flushes pending output on Hijack. Fix: call `ew.stream()` before `hj.Hijack()`.
- [minor] `FEATURE_FLOW.md` is an untracked file in the workspace, outside the listed FILES. Not part of the diff as described. Not reproduced as a defect; the orchestrator should confirm it is intentional.
- [minor] Doc comment says NoCache "must not run before ETag". Consistent with nocache.go stripping If-None-Match, so not a defect. Not reproduced.
=== IMPLEMENTOR HANDOFF 1 (sent after review 1) ===
GOAL: Fix round 1 for middleware/etag.go in /tmp/ff-eval-e6wi4f0f/workspace. The reviewer reproduced two blocking bugs:
1. A handler that calls `WriteHeader(101)` without hijacking: 101 is treated as informational, then finish() writes 200 too ("superfluous WriteHeader"). net/http and middleware/wrap_writer.go treat 101 as a final status. Fix: exclude `http.StatusSwitchingProtocols` from the 1xx informational branch, so 101 is final and non-200 (it streams).
2. Hijack after a buffered Write drops the buffered bytes. Fix it the way net/http does. If a status/body is pending (`ew.wroteHeader` is true, including implicitly via Write), call `ew.stream()` before `hj.Hijack()`. If nothing has been written, do NOT write any status, because a websocket upgrade writes its own raw 101. Just set streaming=true and hijack. Only do either when the underlying writer is a Hijacker. Keep the existing error string otherwise.
Add a regression test for each in middleware/etag_test.go: 101 without hijack over httptest.Server, and Write then Hijack over a real server where the client sees the buffered bytes first. Also make sure an existing or new test covers hijack with nothing written (no 200 leaked before the raw response).

FILES: middleware/etag.go, middleware/etag_test.go. Don't touch anything else.
CONSTRAINTS: stdlib only; minimal change.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. `func ETag(next http.Handler) http.Handler` exists in middleware/etag.go with a doc comment in the repo's style.
2. Methods other than GET and HEAD go straight to `next` with the original ResponseWriter (no wrapping, no buffering, no ETag, no If-None-Match handling).
3. For GET/HEAD with a final status of 200 (explicit WriteHeader(200), or implicit via Write or writing nothing) where the handler did not set an ETag header, a strong ETag is set. It is a quoted string with no W/ prefix, deterministic from the full body (e.g. hex sha256, quoted). Different bodies give different ETags; identical bodies give identical ones. Body, status and the handler's other headers (including a Content-Length it set) are delivered unchanged.
   - Hostile: an empty GET body still gets an ETag (hash of empty). A body written across many small Writes gets the same ETag as one Write. A large body (e.g. 1 MiB) works.
4. HEAD: if the handler wrote body bytes (as GET handlers routed to HEAD do), the ETag is computed from them and no body is sent. If the handler wrote zero bytes on HEAD, no computed ETag is emitted, since the hash of an empty body would be wrong. A handler-set ETag is still kept and used for If-None-Match.
5. A handler-set ETag (strong or W/ weak, any casing of the header key as set via Header().Set) is never overwritten or duplicated.
6. If-None-Match: when the final status is 200 and an ETag is known (computed or handler-set), and any member of If-None-Match weakly matches it (RFC 9110 §8.8.3.2: equal opaque-tags after stripping W/ from both), respond 304. `*` matches any 200 response, even one with no ETag (e.g. HEAD with an empty body). Parse every If-None-Match header line (r.Header.Values), comma-separated with OWS, quote-aware: `"a,b"` is one valid tag because etagc allows commas.
   - Hostile: `W/"x"` vs `"x"` and `"x"` vs `W/"x"` both match. Malformed members (unquoted `x`, a missing closing quote, an empty string, `,,`, a lone `W/`) are skipped without panic and don't stop later valid members matching. `"X"` does not match `"x"`. `*` together with other tags matches. A non-matching list gives a normal 200 with body and ETag.
7. The 304 response has no body, keeps the ETag header and the handler's other headers (Cache-Control, Vary, Set-Cookie, …), and removes Content-Length and Content-Type. 304 applies to both GET and HEAD.
8. Non-200 final statuses (201, 204, 206, 301, 404, 500, …) pass through unchanged: no ETag added, and no 304 even if If-None-Match matches a handler-set ETag. Once a non-200 status is written the middleware streams directly. A second WriteHeader is ignored, like net/http. 1xx informational codes (e.g. WriteHeader(103)) are forwarded immediately and are not the final status.
9. Optional interfaces, as in compress.go: Unwrap() returns the underlying writer, so http.ResponseController works. Hijack forwards or returns the sibling's error string, so websocket upgrades on GET routes behind ETag work. Push forwards or errors the same way. Flush stops buffering: it writes the buffered status, headers and body unchanged (no computed ETag, no 304), flushes, and later writes pass straight through.
   - Hostile: an SSE-style handler that writes, Flushes, writes again gets all bytes in order and no ETag. A Flush before any Write commits 200 with no ETag.
10. The wrapper is per-request (no shared mutable state) and passes `go test -race`.
11. Tests live in middleware/etag_test.go and cover criteria 2-9, including the hostile inputs above.
12. README has the ETag row in the Core middlewares table and the pkg.go.dev link line.
13. `go test -race ./...` and `go vet ./...` pass, and `gofmt -l .` prints nothing.

CHECKS: while working: `go test -race -count=1 -run ETag ./middleware`. At the end: `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .`
